`Claim:` devx@objectstack seat (#6023) · session `session_01UjM2ia8Av1v5NqfqQEQmC6` · R9
Branch `claude/issue-12328-double-slash-refusal-verdicts` · dedicated worktree · model tier: standard.

**Declared file surface:** `scripts/pm/bare-root-worklist.mjs` (its `TRIAGE` map and `--self-test`). Nothing else.

**Serial:** this claim takes the `scripts/pm/bare-root-worklist.mjs` writer slot. ⚠️ PR #12347 merged into this file at 19:51Z, adding the guard that fails the self-test when a recorded verdict sits on a `REACHABLE` row — **cut your worktree from a `main` that contains it**, and read that guard before touching anything.

---

## Zone 1 — rulings (scope, not facts; not renegotiable)

1. The surface above is the whole surface. ⛔ `scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs` is **not** in it — #12299 holds that writer slot this same round.
2. This card is about rows whose **verdicts** rest on a mechanism the tree no longer has. Re-deciding a row is in scope; rewriting a row's `why` prose to say the same thing more nicely is not.
3. ⛔ The map is **shrink-only**. Do not add rows.
4. **Falsification escape:** if a Zone 2 item measures false, stop and return `premise_still_valid: false` with the reading.

## Zone 2 — my assumptions; falsify them before building on them

a. I take the card's claim that **#12300 retired the double-slash refusal** and that 4 `TRIAGE` rows still refuse on it. ⚠️ I have **not** re-read #12300's diff to confirm which mechanism it removed — and I have been wrong about exactly this commit before: I previously read half of #12300's diff and reported on the whole of it. **Read the commit yourself, in full, before trusting the count of 4.**
b. PR #12347's own body states its guard does **not** reach this class ("those four rows never flip to `REACHABLE`, because `covered()` probes a top-of-root path that none of their spellings match"). I have not independently verified that. If #12347 already reaches some of these rows, the remainder is smaller than 4 — measure it.
c. #12289 is `pm:blocked` and concerns two `TRIAGE` rows citing `collapseHint` values the function does not produce. I believe that set is **disjoint** from this card's 4. I have not proven it. If they overlap, say so and stop rather than resolving #12289's rows here.

## Zone 3 — suggested route (not binding)

Read #12300 in full → establish which mechanism actually went away → enumerate the rows whose verdict (not merely prose) is now unsupported → for each, either withdraw the verdict or re-derive it on the current mechanism, naming which. Pin the outcome in `--self-test` so an unsupported verdict cannot land silently again.

Ablate the new assertion both ways, confirm on disk, restore under `trap … EXIT INT TERM`, prove byte-identical with `git hash-object`. Derive the gate union at your final commit; re-derive on `STALE TREE`. Exit codes before any pipe.

## PM correction (error 25) — both Zone 2 items were mine, and both were wrong

The dev returned `premise_still_valid: false` and **stopped without editing anything**. It was right on both counts. I verified each at source rather than taking the report.

### ⭐ Zone 2c — the worst shape on this list so far

I wrote in the dispatch:

> c. #12289 is `pm:blocked` and concerns two `TRIAGE` rows citing `collapseHint` values the function does not produce. I believe that set is **disjoint** from this card's 4. I have not proven it.

It is not disjoint. #12289's row 2 **is** `check:skill-refs SKILLS_DIR skills`, which is row 1 of this card's four.

⭐ **And the record that says so is one I wrote myself.** #12289 carries a STATUS block signed by this seat, dated today, whose own words are:

> The class — this row plus two more found by sweeping — is **#12328**, with the full measured table and options A/B/C.

The card also carries `Blocked-by: #12328` in its body and the `pm:blocked` label — both placed by this seat.

So this was not a missing measurement. **I asserted the opposite of my own written finding, on the same pair of cards, within the same shift.** Every previous entry on this list is some form of *reading too little*; this one is failing to read my own record before contradicting it. That is a worse failure mode, and it is now the standing reason to re-read the linked card's body — not just its labels — before writing a disjointness claim about it.

**Ruling on the dev's open question 2 — delegation confirmed.** This is a reading, not a new decision: #12289 is `pm:blocked`, `Blocked-by: #12328`, its row 1 landed separately as PR #12330 (`cf99875ea8`), its row 2 has no PR and no in-flight writer, and its body hands the class here in as many words. #12328 owns that row. The overlap stops being a stop condition. ⛔ #12289 stays **open** — its unrepaired half must not be hidden behind a closed card.

### Zone 2a — the count of 4 is a material undercount
